chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Zur'at ibn Muhammad, who said:

There was a man in Medina who had a valuable slave girl. So she occurred in the heart of a man and he was fascinated with her. So he complained about that to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: 'Expose yourself to her sight, and every time you see her, say: I ask Allah from His Grace.' So he did.

It was not long before a journey presented itself to her guardian, so he went over to the man and said, 'O so and so! You are my neighbor and the most reliable of the people in my presence, and a journey has presented itself to me, and I would love it if I could leave my so and so slave girl to be with you'. So the man said, 'There is no wife for me nor is there any woman in my house. So how can your slave girl be with me?' So he said, 'I shall evaluate her to you with the price, and you guarantee it for me for her to be with you. So when I come back, sell her and I shall buy her from you, and if you were to attain from her whatever is permissible for you, do it', and he affirmed the price upon him, and the man went out.

So she remained with him for as long as Allah so Desired, until he fulfilled his wishes from her. Then a messenger of one of the Caliphs of the Clan of Umayya came over to buy slave girls for him, so she was among those who had been named for the acquisition. So the governor sent a messenger to him who said to him, 'The slave girl of so and so'. He said, 'So and so is absent'. But he coerced him upon selling her, and gave him the price which had a profit in it.

So when he took the slave girl and went out with her from Medina, her master came over, and the first thing he asked him was that he asked him about the slave girl, how she was. So he informed him with her news and brought out the wealth to him, all of it, which had been evaluated upon him, and which was a profit, and he said, 'This is her price, so take it'. But, the man refused and said, 'I will not take except what I had evaluated upon you, and what was from the excess, so you are welcome to take it for yourself'. Thus, Allah dealt with him by the goodness of his intention.

key_terms.أُقَوِّمُهَا: I shall evaluate her (set a price)

ai.seo_question: What is the story of the man and the slave girl in Al-Kafi regarding sincerity and financial ethics?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Shia concept of *Ihsan* (excellence in conduct) and the spiritual efficacy of specific dhikr in purifying desire, as advised by Imam al-Sadiq (AS). The narrative highlights the virtue of sincerity (*ikhlas*) in financial transactions, where the man’s refusal to keep the windfall profit demonstrates that his initial guardianship was for Allah’s sake rather than mere opportunity, a principle often cited in Shia ethical jurisprudence.
